issue: Known on 1979-83 RX-7s (bulletin 016/85): the rear harness is cut by a sharp metal edge where it runs inside the rear body, shorting or opening circuits. Symptoms by what blew: RADIO/ANTENNA fuse - radio and antenna dead; TAIL/ILLUM - tail, head, licence and illumination lamps out; METER/BACK - meters, warning lamps and back-up lamps out; OPENER - fuel door release dead; an open circuit - rear defroster or rear wiper dead; a short - rear wiper runs with its switch OFF. Factory fix: repair the harness and wrap it in foam rubber; the routing changed from July 1984 (S-046)
status: Not known on this car; look at the harness where the bulletin's figure shows it near the rear wheel arch when the rear trim is off - the rear defroster and hatch faults (K-016, K-020, K-026) make it worth a look
impact: Blown fuses and dead rear circuits that come back after a fuse is replaced

issue: Known on 1979-84 RX-7s (bulletin 012/85): the ENGINE fuse blows and the engine will not start because the engine harness shorts where it runs by the thermostat and the air hose to the air cleaner. Factory fix: repair the harness; the clearance was increased from October 1984 (S-046)
status: Not known on this car; check that spot first if the ENGINE fuse is found blown (the car's no-start, K-025, is not yet diagnosed)
impact: No start

issue: Design trait of the FB rear suspension (S-053): the upper trailing links swing the axle sideways in roll while the Watt link holds it to a vertical path, and the axle rotates about a short side-view swing arm - the bushings bind, so rear roll stiffness rises with roll angle (sudden oversteer over a bump at the limit). Lowering the car shortens the swing arm (about 28 in at stock height, 17.5 in lowered) and worsens it; spherical joints in the Watt link or a rod-end panhard make the bind worse, and all-spherical bushings leave the body to twist instead
status: A trait of every FB, not a fault of this car; it bears on the bushing overhaul (K-005): keep compliant rubber bushings and the stock ride height unless the geometry is corrected as a whole
impact: Handling at the limit; bushing wear
